passage:
During evening football in the colony lane, Imran and Zayn picked teams. One by one the group shrank, until only Tushar stood by the lamp post. “Guess I'm the leftover!” Tushar said, laughing loudly and kicking a stone. His ears were red.

Zayn shrugged. “You can have him, Imran.”

Imran looked at Tushar. “We got the best one for last. Tushar, you're on defence, because you never give up.” Tushar's shoulders came down a little.

When the match began, the stone was still in his pocket.

qa.q: Where did Tushar stand while waiting to be picked?
qa.a: Tushar stood by the lamp post.

qa.q: Why did Tushar laugh loudly and say he was the leftover?
qa.a: Tushar felt hurt at being picked last and laughed it off to hide the sting, as the red ears suggest.

qa.q: What did Imran say that helped Tushar?
qa.a: Imran said the best one was picked last and gave Tushar a place in defence because Tushar never gives up.

qa.q: What might Zayn have been thinking when saying, “You can have him, Imran”?
qa.a: Zayn probably cared about winning and saw Tushar as weak, without thinking how the words landed on a child waiting in public.

grounding: A child left until the end of team selection laughs it off, and a kind captain picks them warmly.

passage:
“Last one,” said Ritu, counting. “Manjula.”

“Ha, I'm always the bonus,” Manjula said, tugging her braid. Nobody laughed.

Salma, captain of Team Blue, stepped forward. “Manjula, come here. I've been saving you.”

“For what?”

“The goal circle. You never lose track of where the ball is. Last time you shouted ‘left!’ and we scored.”

“I only did that once.”

“Once was enough.” Salma nudged her shoulder. “Stand by me.”

Manjula stepped over slowly, hiding a smile. “Okay. But if I mess up, I go back to being the bonus.”

“Deal,” said Salma. “You won't.”

qa.q: What did Manjula call herself when picked last?
qa.a: Manjula said, “I'm always the bonus.”

qa.q: Why did Manjula say she was always the bonus while tugging the braid?
qa.a: Manjula was hiding hurt behind a joke, and tugging the braid shows nervousness about being measured in public.

qa.q: What did Salma do that changed how Manjula felt?
qa.a: Salma called Manjula over warmly, said Manjula had been saved for the goal circle and named a real contribution.

qa.q: What might Salma have noticed that led Salma to choose Manjula for the goal circle?
qa.a: Salma noticed that Manjula tracks the ball well and once shouted “left!” to set up a goal, a strength others had missed.

grounding: A child picked last feels their worth measured in public and laughs it off, and a kind captain picks them warmly.

passage:
“Ganga, you're with us,” said the captain, last of all, when there was nobody else left.
Ganga laughed loudly. “Lucky you! You got the best player for free!” A few kids giggled.
Walking to the kho-kho line, she kicked a stone hard.
Next Friday, Vaibhav was captain.
“Ganga,” he said first, smiling. “You're fast when you dodge. I want you.”
“Me? First?”
“Yes, you.”
Ganga blinked. “Okay.” She ran to his side so fast she almost tripped.
That game, she dodged four chasers in a row. Vaibhav clapped the loudest.

qa.q: How many chasers did Ganga dodge in a row?
qa.a: Four chasers in a row.

qa.q: What was Ganga feeling when she kicked the stone?
qa.a: She was hurt and embarrassed at being picked last, even though she laughed it off out loud.

qa.q: What did Vaibhav do that undid much of the hurt?
qa.a: He picked Ganga first, warmly, and named a real strength, which made her feel valued.

qa.q: How might the first captain feel seeing Ganga dodge four chasers?
qa.a: They might feel surprised and a little sheepish, realising they overlooked a good player.

grounding: Shows a child picked last who laughs it off, and a kind captain who picks her first warmly, undoing much of the hurt.

passage:
I'm Charu, and I was always picked last for throwball in Class 5.
Every time, I'd stand there while the names were called. Rekha, Divya, Seema... Charu. Everyone would look at me. I'd make a joke, like, “Saving the best for last!” and everyone laughed. Then I'd go home and not want to eat.
One day Ankita became captain. She looked at the line and said, “Charu first. You never drop a throw.”
I didn't even move for a second.
I did drop one throw that day, but Ankita just shouted, “Next one!” I played better than I had all year.
I still remember that day more than any match we won.

qa.q: What sport was Charu always picked last for?
qa.a: Throwball.

qa.q: How did Charu feel after the jokes when getting home?
qa.a: Charu felt hurt and sad, not wanting to eat, even after laughing it off in front of everyone.

qa.q: What did Ankita do that made such a difference?
qa.a: Ankita picked Charu first, warmly, and named a strength, and stayed kind after a mistake, which undid much of the hurt.

qa.q: How might the others have seen Charu's jokes?
qa.a: They probably thought Charu didn't mind, since Charu made them laugh, not realising the hurt underneath.

grounding: A child recalls being picked last and laughing it off, until a kind captain picked Charu first warmly and undid much of the hurt.

passage:
PE teacher's note, Class 6, Thursday.
For weeks, Rafiq has been the last child chosen in every team game. He jokes about it (“I'm the secret weapon!”), but today I saw him sitting alone on the bench afterwards, rubbing his eyes.
Today Damini was one of the captains. She picked Rafiq first, and said clearly, “You're good at blocking.” The whole line went quiet. Rafiq stood up straight and walked over with a huge grin. He played the whole game with energy.
From next week, I will use numbered cards to make teams, and give each team a captain who changes weekly. I will thank Damini privately.

qa.q: What does Rafiq joke that he is?
qa.a: "The secret weapon."

qa.q: What does Rafiq rubbing his eyes on the bench suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he feels hurt and humiliated by always being picked last, even though he jokes about it.

qa.q: Why does the teacher's new plan make sense?
qa.a: Numbered cards and rotating captains stop public ranking, so no child is left to be picked last every week.

qa.q: How might Damini have felt when the line went quiet?
qa.a: She was probably a little nervous but sure of her choice, glad to see Rafiq grin.

grounding: A PE teacher notes a child always picked last who jokes about it, and how a kind captain choosing him first changed his day.

passage:
Dear Diary,
Today at PT, team picking again. I stood on the line while names got called: Rahul, Vicky, Sam, everyone. My shoes got really interesting.
When three of us were left, I joked about being "saved for last like the best sweet". Everybody laughed. I laughed too, even though my stomach felt like a stone.
Then Joseph, captain of the blue side, said, "Anirban! I wanted you. You always pass instead of hogging." He said it like he meant it, and gave me a high five.
I passed to him twice and he scored once. At lunch he sat next to me.
Maybe I'm not bad at football. Maybe I'm just not fast.
Anirban

qa.q: What did Anirban joke about being saved for last like?
qa.a: Like the best sweet.

qa.q: How did Anirban feel while making the joke?
qa.a: Anirban felt hurt and embarrassed, stomach "like a stone", and used the joke to hide it.

qa.q: How could the PT teacher make team picking kinder?
qa.a: Make teams by counting off or drawing names, so nobody has to stand on a line waiting to be chosen.

qa.q: Why might Joseph have picked Anirban so warmly?
qa.a: Joseph seems to value passing, and may have seen how the waiting hurt, so he made Anirban feel wanted.

grounding: Shows a child left until the end of team picking who laughs it off while hurting, and a kind captain whose warm pick eases the sting.
